To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed a three-stage search pipeline to find and characterize supermassive black hole binaries in LISA, and that we have demonstrated its performance using simulated LISA data.

we have developed a three-stage data analysis pipeline for detecting and estimating the parameters of supermassive binary black hole systems in LISA data and have demonstrated that the pipeline works as designed.

we have developed and tested an analysis pipeline for the detection of SMBH-binary sources in LISA data, and that we have demonstrated the feasibility of this pipeline in the context of the first Mock LISAData Challenge.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of data analysis methods for gravitational wave detection and measurement with LISA, and in particular with the development of a pipeline for searching for supermassive binary black holes in LISA data.
the search and parameter estimation for supermassive binary black-hole signals in the data of the Laser Interferometric Space Antenna (eLISA), a space-based gravitational wave detector.
the detection and characterization of the gravitational waves from supermassive black hole binaries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper presents an excellent analysis pipeline for the detection and measurement of the parameters for supermassive binary black holes in LISA data and that this analysis pipeline has been demonstrated to work well on simulated data.
the data analysis pipeline presented here is capable of finding and estimating the parameters of supermassive binary black holes in simulated LISA data.

the LISA data analysis pipeline for SMBH-binary detection and characterization has been developed to a level where the pipeline will be able to detect and characterize SMBH-binary sources in LISA data, provided the LISA noise curve meets the design specifications and provided that no unexpected data analysis challenges emerge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a robust pipeline that can search and detect SMBH-binary signals from LISA data.
the pipeline can recover the parameters of simulated SMBH binaries with a signal-to-noise ratio as low as 10.
our pipeline is able to find and estimate the parameters of a simulated SMBH binary with a false alarm rate of 0.1 per year in a 4-year LISA mission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a three-stage search pipeline is feasible and can be used to measure the parameters of a SMBH binary in a few hours of computer time on a single processor.
a pipeline with a three-stage data analysis is feasible for LISA data and will be necessary for extracting the most information from LISA data.
the first stage of our search pipeline is sufficiently sensitive that the second stage is able to find all the signals in the simulated data.
